A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cold shock response of E. coli includes a novel acyltransferase activity which transfers palmitoleoy1 from ACP to lipid A. This

The main takeaway from our work is that
the cold shock response of E. coli involves a major reprogramming of lipid A biosynthesis, with the appearance of palmitoyl-ACP and palmitoleate as the predominant fatty acyl chains in lipid A.
the cold-induced acyltransferase is specific for palmitoyl-ACP, which is the major fatty acid in E. coli grown at 12 C.
the cold shock-induced lpxP-encoded palmitoleoylation of the lipid A precursor KDO2-lipid IV(A) is the first example of the use of an ACP-dependent acyltransferase to modify a lipid A precursor.
